findings.what: lrgDlgClass runs lrgDlgIsBackOut(text) on the ENTRY with an unanchored 'not sure|nothing|never mind' test, so Gunmar's quest line 'We're not sure, but they have an Elder Scroll.' (scripted+goodbye, A New Order -> 45) is class 'back': the fast path never executes it ('they have an Elder Scroll' -> nothing) and a model LEAVE clicks it. Index-wide 885 entry-side back lines, 64 of them scripted and not goodbye (e.g. MQ204 'I have nothing to hide. The Blades helped me find out about it.').

findings.hits: Chasing Echoes (every player who chooses to be turned)
findings.what: lrgDlgClauseStarts breaks clauses on , ; : and dashes but not on . ! ?, so in 'I don't see another way. I'll become a vampire.' the first sentence's negator negates 'become vampire': 'I'll become a vampire' (0.85 containment) is blocked by negation parity.

findings.hits: A New Order, Prophet (Dawnguard); 50 index norms start with we're
findings.what: lrgDlgFoldTokens turns we're into 'were', a question word in lrgDlgLeadsQuestion: every We're-statement (entry or utterance) is read as a question. Sorine's single 'We're meeting at Fort Dawnguard' rejects the statement 'meet us at Fort Dawnguard'; Gunmar's 'We're up against vampires' releases on 'are you afraid of vampires?'.
